shlokas.sanskrit: विसृज्य च महाबाहुर्ऋक्षवानरराक्षसान् । भ्रातृभिः सहितो रामः प्रमुमोद सुखं सुखी ।। 7.41.1 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: visṛjya ca mahābāhurṛkṣavānararākṣasān | bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito rāmaḥ pramumoda sukhaṃ sukhī || 7.41.1 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having dismissed the bears, vanaras, and Rakshasas, the mighty-armed Rama, together with his brothers, rejoiced in happiness, himself contented.

shlokas.sanskrit: अथापराह्णसमये भ्रातृभिः सह राघवः । शुश्राव मधुरां वाणीमन्तरिक्षात् प्रभाषिताम् ।। 7.41.2 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: athāparāhṇasamaye bhrātṛbhiḥ saha rāghavaḥ | śuśrāva madhurāṃ vāṇīmantarikṣāt prabhāṣitām || 7.41.2 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then, in the afternoon hours, Raghava, in the company of his brothers, heard a sweet voice spoken from the sky.

shlokas.sanskrit: सौम्य राम निरीक्षस्व सौम्येन वदनेन माम् । कुबेरभवनात्प्राप्तं विद्धि मां पुष्पकं प्रभो ।। 7.41.3 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: saumya rāma nirīkṣasva saumyena vadanena mām | kuberabhavanātprāptaṃ viddhi māṃ puṣpakaṃ prabho || 7.41.3 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "O gentle Rama, look upon me with a kindly face. Know me, O lord, to be the Pushpaka, come back from the abode of Kubera."

shlokas.sanskrit: तव शासनमाज्ञाय गतो ऽस्मि भवनं प्रति । उपस्थातुं नरश्रेष्ठ स च मां प्रत्यभाषत ।। 7.41.4 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tava śāsanamājñāya gato 'smi bhavanaṃ prati | upasthātuṃ naraśreṣṭha sa ca māṃ pratyabhāṣata || 7.41.4 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "Having understood your command, O best of men, I went to that abode to attend upon him; and he, in turn, spoke to me thus:"

shlokas.sanskrit: निर्जितस्त्वं नरेन्द्रेण राघवेण महात्मना । निहत्य युधि दुर्धर्षं रावणं राक्षसेश्वरम् ।। 7.41.5 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: nirjitastvaṃ narendreṇa rāghaveṇa mahātmanā | nihatya yudhi durdharṣaṃ rāvaṇaṃ rākṣaseśvaram || 7.41.5 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "You have been won by the king, the great-souled Raghava, who slew in battle the unassailable Ravana, the lord of the Rakshasas."

shlokas.sanskrit: ममापि परमा प्रीतर्हते तस्मिन्दुरात्मनि । रावणे सगणे चैव सपुत्रे सहबान्धवे ।। 7.41.6 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: mamāpi paramā prītarhate tasmindurātmani | rāvaṇe sagaṇe caiva saputre sahabāndhave || 7.41.6 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "To me also there is the greatest joy, now that this wicked-souled one has been slain — Ravana, together with his hosts, his sons, and his kinsmen."

shlokas.sanskrit: स त्वं रामेण लङ्कायां निर्जितः परमात्मना । वह सौम्य तमेव त्वमहमाज्ञापयामि ते ।। 7.41.7 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: sa tvaṃ rāmeṇa laṅkāyāṃ nirjitaḥ paramātmanā | vaha saumya tameva tvamahamājñāpayāmi te || 7.41.7 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "You were conquered by Rama, the Supreme Self, in Lanka. Therefore carry that very one, O gentle one; this I command you."

shlokas.sanskrit: परमो ह्येष मे कामो यत्त्वं राघवनन्दनम् । वहेर्लोकस्य संयानं गच्छस्व विगतज्वरः ।। 7.41.8 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: paramo hyeṣa me kāmo yattvaṃ rāghavanandanam | vaherlokasya saṃyānaṃ gacchasva vigatajvaraḥ || 7.41.8 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "For this is my highest wish — that you should carry the delight of the Raghus, you who are the conveyance of the world. Go, free from all distress."

shlokas.sanskrit: सो ऽहं शासनमाज्ञाय धनदस्य महात्मनः । त्वत्सकाशमनुप्राप्तो निर्विशङ्कः प्रतीक्ष माम् ।। 7.41.9 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: so 'haṃ śāsanamājñāya dhanadasya mahātmanaḥ | tvatsakāśamanuprāpto nirviśaṅkaḥ pratīkṣa mām || 7.41.9 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "And so I, having received the command of the great-souled Giver of Wealth, have come into your presence. Without any misgiving, await me."

shlokas.sanskrit: अदृष्यः सर्वभूतानां सर्वेषां धनदाज्ञया । चराम्यहं प्रभावेण तवाज्ञां परिपालयन् ।। 7.41.10 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: adṛṣyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ sarveṣāṃ dhanadājñayā | carāmyahaṃ prabhāveṇa tavājñāṃ paripālayan || 7.41.10 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "By the order of the Giver of Wealth, invisible to all beings, I move about by my own power, fulfilling your command."

shlokas.sanskrit: एवमुक्तस्तदा रामः पुष्पकेण महाबलः । उवाच पुष्पकं दृष्ट्वा विमानं पुनरागतम् ।। 7.41.11 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: evamuktastadā rāmaḥ puṣpakeṇa mahābalaḥ | uvāca puṣpakaṃ dṛṣṭvā vimānaṃ punarāgatam || 7.41.11 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Thus addressed by the Pushpaka, the mighty Rama then, beholding the chariot Pushpaka come back again, spoke to it.

shlokas.sanskrit: यद्येवं स्वागतं ते ऽस्तु विमानवर पुष्पक । आनुकूल्याद्धनेशस्य वृत्तदोषो न नो भवेत् ।। 7.41.12 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: yadyevaṃ svāgataṃ te 'stu vimānavara puṣpaka | ānukūlyāddhaneśasya vṛttadoṣo na no bhavet || 7.41.12 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "If it be so, then welcome to you, O Pushpaka, best of chariots. Through compliance with the Lord of Wealth, let no fault of conduct fall upon us."

shlokas.sanskrit: लाजैश्चैव तथा पुष्पैर्धूपैश्चैव सुगन्धिभिः । पूजयित्वा महाबाहू राघवः पुष्पकं तदा ।। 7.41.13 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: lājaiścaiva tathā puṣpairdhūpaiścaiva sugandhibhiḥ | pūjayitvā mahābāhū rāghavaḥ puṣpakaṃ tadā || 7.41.13 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then the mighty-armed Raghava, having worshipped the Pushpaka with parched grain, with flowers, and with fragrant incense,

shlokas.sanskrit: गम्यतामिति चोवाच आगच्छ त्वं स्मरे यदा । सिद्धानां च गतौ सौम्य मा विषादेन योजय । प्रतिघातश्च ते मा भूद्यथेष्टं गच्छतो दिशः ।। 7.41.14 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: gamyatāmiti covāca āgaccha tvaṃ smare yadā | siddhānāṃ ca gatau saumya mā viṣādena yojaya | pratighātaśca te mā bhūdyatheṣṭaṃ gacchato diśaḥ || 7.41.14 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: said, "You may go; and come when I remember you. In the path of the perfected ones, O gentle one, do not give yourself to despair; let there be no obstruction for you as you travel to whatever quarters you wish."

shlokas.sanskrit: एवमस्त्विति रामेण पूजयित्वा विसर्जितम् । अभिप्रेतां दिशं तस्मात्प्रायात्तत्पुष्पकं तदा ।। 7.41.15 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: evamastviti rāmeṇa pūjayitvā visarjitam | abhipretāṃ diśaṃ tasmātprāyāttatpuṣpakaṃ tadā || 7.41.15 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "So be it" — thus honored and dismissed by Rama, that Pushpaka then set out from there toward the quarter it desired.

shlokas.sanskrit: एवमन्तर्हिते तस्मिन्पुष्पके सुकृतात्मनि । भरतः प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यमुवाच रघुनन्दनम् ।। 7.41.16 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: evamantarhite tasminpuṣpake sukṛtātmani | bharataḥ prāñjalirvākyamuvāca raghunandanam || 7.41.16 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: When the Pushpaka of meritorious nature had thus vanished, Bharata, with joined palms, spoke these words to the delight of the Raghus.

shlokas.sanskrit: विविधात्मनि दृश्यन्ते त्वयि वीर प्रशासति । अमानुषाणां सत्त्वानां व्याहृतानि मुहुर्मुहुः ।। 7.41.17 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: vividhātmani dṛśyante tvayi vīra praśāsati | amānuṣāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ vyāhṛtāni muhurmuhuḥ || 7.41.17 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: O hero, while you rule, beings of various kinds are seen, and again and again the utterances of non-human creatures are heard.

shlokas.sanskrit: अनामयश्च सत्वानां साग्रो मासो गतो ह्ययम् । जीर्णानामपि सत्त्वानां मृत्युर्नायाति राघव ।। 7.41.18 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: anāmayaśca satvānāṃ sāgro māso gato hyayam | jīrṇānāmapi sattvānāṃ mṛtyurnāyāti rāghava || 7.41.18 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: A full month and more has now passed without sickness among living beings; and even among the aged, O Raghava, death does not come.

shlokas.sanskrit: अरोगप्रसवा नार्यो वपुष्मन्तो हि मानवाः । हर्षश्चाभ्यधिको राजञ्जनस्य पुरवासिनः ।। 7.41.19 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: arogaprasavā nāryo vapuṣmanto hi mānavāḥ | harṣaścābhyadhiko rājañjanasya puravāsinaḥ || 7.41.19 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Women give birth free of disease, and men are robust of body; and the joy of the city-dwelling people, O king, is exceedingly great.

shlokas.sanskrit: काले वर्षति पर्जन्यः पातयन्नमृतं पयः । वाताश्चापि प्रवान्त्येते स्पर्शयुक्ताः सुखाः शिवाः ।। 7.41.20 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: kāle varṣati parjanyaḥ pātayannamṛtaṃ payaḥ | vātāścāpi pravāntyete sparśayuktāḥ sukhāḥ śivāḥ || 7.41.20 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: The rain-cloud pours down in its proper season, sending down water like nectar; and the winds too blow pleasant to the touch, comfortable and auspicious.

shlokas.sanskrit: ईदृशो ऽनश्वरो राजा भवेदिति नरेश्वरः । कथयन्ति पुरे राजन्पौरजानपदास्तथा ।। 7.41.21 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: īdṛśo 'naśvaro rājā bhavediti nareśvaraḥ | kathayanti pure rājanpaurajānapadāstathā || 7.41.21 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "May such a king, this lord of men, be imperishable" — thus, O king, the townsfolk and country-folk speak in the city.

shlokas.sanskrit: एता वाचः सुमधुरा भरतेन समीरिताः । श्रुत्वा रामो मुदा युक्तो बभूव नृपसत्तमः ।। 7.41.22 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: etā vācaḥ sumadhurā bharatena samīritāḥ | śrutvā rāmo mudā yukto babhūva nṛpasattamaḥ || 7.41.22 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Hearing these very sweet words spoken by Bharata, Rama, the best of kings, was filled with joy.

shlokas.sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकचत्वारिंशः सर्गः ।। 41 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmaduttarakāṇḍe ekacatvāriṃśaḥ sargaḥ || 41 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Thus ends the forty-first sarga in the venerable Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana, the first poem composed by the sage Valmiki.
